order_book: Order book and execution visibility: As of September 30th, 2026, our order book stood at approximately INR2,543 crores, comprising approximately INR1,303 crores from manufacturing, INR1,240 crores from EPC.

In order book front, as on September 30, 2026, our total order book stood approximately at INR2,543 crores, comprising approximately INR1,303 crores from our manufacturing and INR1,240 crores from EPC.
And my second question was regarding -- there's an order pipeline that was discussed in the previous quarter around INR1,250 plus crores in order pipeline that is expected.
guidance: Having covered our H1 performance, let me briefly share our outlook for H2.
Looking ahead, we expect EBITDA margin to stabilize in the range of 12.5% to 13%.
capex: To sum up this half of the year marks Laser's entry into transmission with commercial HTLS and 220 kV underground credentials, supported by a clear plan to enhance capacity.

MD sir has outlined how Laser Power has entered the transmission business through our first HTLS order from Power Grid, our first 220 kV underground project from CESC, and the planned expansion at Kharagpur.
risks: Through our licensing agreement with TS Conductors USA, we have access to advanced conductor technology design to address the practical challenges the utilities face.
The moderation in EPC revenue was primarily attributed to execution delays caused by heavy rains in the areas of project.
focus: We are also targeting improvement of approximately 25 to 40 days in working capital days by Q4 FY27.
Divyesh Sheth: I also just wanted to understand, moving forward, are we more focused on conductors than cables, or there would be a similar mix moving forward?
